Analysis.description: An analysis: the files it reads, the artefacts it makes and the decisions it makes along the way. It is the content of an `astra.yaml` file.

analyses.description: The analyses this analysis uses, keyed by the id it addresses them by.

decisions.description: The choices the analysis makes, keyed by id.

description.description: Free-prose description of this analysis — the same optional field every other content object carries (Input, Output, Option, Universe). A short human orientation lives here; richer write-ups (figures, citations, multi-page reports) are authored externally and reference analysis elements by address rather than restating them.

findings.description: What the analysis concludes, as insights keyed by id.

inputs.description: The files the analysis reads, keyed by id.

outputs.description: The artefacts the analysis makes, and its switches, keyed by id.

prior_insights.description: What earlier work establishes and the analysis builds on, as insights keyed by id. Options cite them in their `insights`.

spec_version.description: The version of the ASTRA specification the document is written against, such as `0.1.0`.

universes.description: The universes of the analysis, and the universes of other analyses it imports, keyed by id. An import has an `analysis` and a `universe`.

Analysis.title: Analysis

AnalysisDeclaration__identifier_optional.description: An analysis that this analysis uses, found by exactly one of `path` and `url`. Its elements are addressed through the declaration's id, as `<declaration>.<element>`.

commit.description: The full id of the commit the declared analysis is read at. A declaration with a `url` has one; with a `path`, it declares the analysis at that path as it was at that commit.

path.description: The directory of the declared analysis's `astra.yaml`, relative to the folder of this `astra.yaml`, with `/` between folders. It is non-empty and doesn't start with `/`.

url.description: Where git fetches another repository from, as a remote with no ASCII space or control character, in one of two forms: `scheme://` and at least one character, where the scheme is an ASCII letter followed by any ASCII letters, digits, `+`, `.` and `-`, such as `https://example.org/remote.git` or `file:///srv/remote.git`; or scp-like, `[user@]host:path`, where `host`, `path` and any `user` are non-empty, `user` and `host` hold no `/`, `@` or `:`, and the value doesn't start with a scheme and `://`, such as `git@example.org:remote.git`. The declared analysis is the one at the top level of that repository, at `commit`.

AnalysisDeclaration__identifier_optional.title: AnalysisDeclaration

AnalysisEntry.description: One analysis, the driving analysis or one it declares, directly or not: its identity, its file as written and where its declarations lead. Its file is `astra.yaml` in `folder`.

commit.description: The full id of the commit the analysis is read at. Left out for the working tree.

declares.description: For each entry of the analysis's `analyses`, the identity of the analysis it leads to, itself an entry of the document's `analyses`.

fields.description: The content of the analysis's `astra.yaml`, exactly as written.

folder.description: The analysis's folder, as a path. The top of the tree is the empty string.

url.description: The remote the analysis is read from, for an analysis declared with a `url` or reached through one.

AnalysisEntry.title: AnalysisEntry

Citation.description: A planned result that an item of evidence cites.

result.description: The result cited, as its index in the document's `results`.

universe.description: The id of the universe of the driving analysis in which this result is the one cited. Left out for pinned evidence and for evidence that cites an output built once.

Citation.title: Citation

Decision__identifier_optional.description: A choice the analysis makes between options, such as which method to use.

options.description: The options the decision chooses between, keyed by id. There is at least one.

Decision__identifier_optional.title: Decision

DeclaredAnalysis__identifier_optional.description: The analysis one declaration leads to, written in an entry's `declares` as `<declaration>: <identity>`.

commit.description: The full id of the commit the analysis is read at. Left out for the working tree.

folder.description: The analysis's folder, as a path. The top of the tree is the empty string.

DeclaredAnalysis__identifier_optional.title: DeclaredAnalysis

ElementRef.description: What names an element of an analysis: the analysis and the element's id there. The kind of element follows from the field that holds the reference.

analysis.description: The analysis the element is in.

id.description: The element's id in that analysis.

ElementRef.title: ElementRef

Evidence.description: What a claim rests on: a published work, cited by its `doi`, or an output, cited as an `artifact`. It has exactly one of the two, and a `version` only with a `doi`.

artifact.description: A reference to the cited output, written as in an output's `inputs`. It may pin the output to a universe, the one the claim is about, such as `output1#u1`. A switch is cited as the case it takes, and each of its cases names an output other than a switch, or a switch like it.

doi.description: The DOI name of the cited work, under the `10` directory: `10.`, the registrant code, `/` and a non-empty suffix, such as `10.5555/12345678`.

location.description: The place in the cited work or output the claim rests on, such as `page=6`.

quote.description: The passage of the cited work or output the claim rests on. With a `location`, the passage is sought within that place.

version.description: The version of the cited work, counted from 1, such as `2` for the second version of an arXiv paper.

Evidence.title: Evidence

EvidenceEntry.description: An item of evidence that cites an output, and the results it cites.

analysis.description: The analysis whose file holds the item.

cites.description: The planned results the item cites, through any switch and pin: one with no `universe`, or one for each universe of the driving analysis that has a result to cite, in those universes' order.

pointer.description: A JSON Pointer to the item in that analysis's `fields`, such as `/findings/insight1/evidence/0`.

EvidenceEntry.title: EvidenceEntry

FragmentSelector.description: A place in the cited work or output, given as a fragment identifier in the syntax `conforms_to` names, such as `row=5-7` in a CSV (RFC 7111). Without `conforms_to`, it is a PDF fragment identifier (RFC 8118 §3), such as `page=6`, with pages counted from 1.

conforms_to.description: The IRI of the specification of the fragment syntax `value` follows, as W3C Web Annotation gives it, such as `http://tools.ietf.org/rfc/rfc7111` for a CSV. Without it, `value` is a PDF fragment identifier (RFC 8118).

value.description: The fragment identifier, without the leading `#`, such as `page=6`. It is non-empty, holds no ASCII space or control character and none of `"`, `#`, `<`, `>`, `[`, the backslash, `]`, `^`, the backtick, `{`, `|` and `}`, and has `%` only before two hex digits.

FragmentSelector.title: FragmentSelector

Identity.description: What names an analysis: its folder and the commit it is read at. One folder at one commit is one analysis, however it is declared.

commit.description: The full id of the commit the analysis is read at. Left out for the working tree.

folder.description: The analysis's folder, as a path. The top of the tree is the empty string.

Identity.title: Identity

Input__identifier_optional.description: A file the analysis reads, tracked in git with it and named by its path.

label.description: Short human-readable name for compact rendering (margin glyphs, breadcrumbs, card titles). Optional; tooling falls back to id when absent.

path.description: The path of the input's file, relative to the folder of the `astra.yaml`, with `/` between folders. It is non-empty and doesn't start with `/`.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the input.

Input__identifier_optional.title: Input

Insight__identifier_optional.description: A unit of scientific knowledge backed by evidence. Used for both prior_insights (informing decisions) and findings (conclusions from the analysis).

description.description: The reasoning behind the claim, in free prose.

evidence.description: What the claim rests on, as a list. There is at least one.

label.description: Short human-readable name for compact rendering (margin glyphs, breadcrumbs, card titles). Optional; tooling falls back to id when absent.

Insight__identifier_optional.title: Insight

Location.description: Where a diagnostic or a note is: a file, and a place in it.

column.description: The column of the place in its line, counted from 1.

commit.description: The full id of the commit the file is read at. Left out for the working tree.

file.description: The file's path from the top of the repository that holds it.

key.description: The map key or field named at the place.

line.description: The line of the place in the file, counted from 1.

pointer.description: A JSON Pointer to the place in the file. The whole file is the empty string.

url.description: The remote the file is read from, if any.

Location.title: Location

Note.description: Something an author may want to tidy, which breaks no rule.

built.description: Whether the note concerns what the driving analysis builds.

location.description: The pin, the output or the command the note is about.

results.description: The planned results the note is about, each as its index in the document's `results`.

Note.title: Note

Option__identifier_optional.description: One of the options a decision chooses between.

excluded.description: Why the option is ruled out. An option with a reason is excluded: no effective selection selects it.

incompatible_with.description: The options that are never selected together with this option, among the decisions a universe uses.

insights.description: The ids of the prior insights that support the option.

requires.description: The options that are also selected wherever this option is, among the decisions a universe uses: a decision it doesn't use selects none.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the option.

Option__identifier_optional.title: Option

OutputType.description: The kind of artefact an output is.
OutputType.title: OutputType

Output__identifier_optional.description: An entry of `outputs`: an artefact the analysis makes, such as a metric, a figure or a table, with what it is, what it is made from and how; or a switch, which has a `switch` and `cases`, makes nothing, and is read as the case it takes.

additionalProperties.description: A reference to the input, output or switch the switch is read as where the option is selected, written as an entry of an output's `inputs` is, such as `stage.output3` or `output1#u1`.

cases.description: For a switch, what it is read as where its decision selects each option that has a case, as `<option>: <reference>`, such as `b: stage.output3`. There is at least one, and several options can name one reference. Where its decision selects an option with no case, the switch isn't built, nor is anything that reads it without a pin.

decisions.description: The addresses of the decisions whose option the output is made with directly, not through what it reads: a different option for any of them, in the universe being built, can give a different result.

format.description: How the output's artefact is encoded, as a lowercase token: the extension of its results' files, without the leading dot, such as `png`, `csv` or `parquet`. Every output but a switch has one.

inputs.description: What the output is made from, in order: references to inputs and outputs of the analysis or of analyses it declares, a switch read as the case it takes. A reference can be pinned to a universe with `#`.

label.description: Short human-readable name for compact rendering (margin glyphs, breadcrumbs, card titles). Optional; tooling falls back to id when absent.

recipe.description: How the output is made. Every output but a switch has one.

switch.description: For a switch, the address of the decision whose selected option picks the case it takes, such as `decision1` or `stage.decision2`.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the output.

type.description: The kind of artefact the output is. Every output but a switch has one.

Output__identifier_optional.title: Output

Place.description: Where one name of a planned result puts it, in the folder of the analysis the result belongs to.

address.description: The name, then, for a result built in a universe, `#` and that universe's own id, such as `stage.output3#u1`. With the result's `owner`, it names the result.

bytes.description: The path of the default place of the result's bytes.

name.description: The result's name: its output's id after the ids of the driven declarations that lead to it from the analysis it belongs to, such as `stage.output3`.

record.description: The path of the result's record at the place.

Place.title: Place

Read.description: One entry of an output's `inputs`, and what a planned result reads through it: an input's file, or another planned result's bytes. It has exactly one of `input` and `result`.

commit.description: The full id of the commit `path` is read at. Left out for the working tree.

entry.description: The entry exactly as the output's `inputs` lists it.

path.description: The path of the file read: the input's file, or the default place of the bytes of the result read.

result.description: The planned result read, as its index in the document's `results`, always smaller than the index of the result that reads it.

through.description: The switches the entry reads through, the outermost first. Left out where the entry names no switch.

Read.title: Read

Recipe.description: How an output is made: a `command` and the compute `resources` it asks for. What the output is made from and the decisions it is made with are the output's `inputs` and `decisions`; the command reaches the inputs and decisions through its placeholders.

command.description:
The POSIX shell command that makes the output, such as `python src/output1.py`. It is a template. Read from the left, `{{` stands for a literal `{` and `}}` for a literal `}`, and any other `{` opens a placeholder, which ends at the next `}`. A runner substitutes each placeholder, and each `{{` and `}}`, before running the command:

  {inputs.<entry>}     the path of what an entry of the output's
                       `inputs` names (for a switch, what the case
                       it takes names), with <entry> written
                       exactly as the entry is, dots and `#`
                       included, as in
                       {inputs.subanalysis.output1#u1}
  {decisions.<entry>}  the id of the option selected for the
                       decision an entry of the output's
                       `decisions` names, with <entry> written
                       exactly as the entry is, as in
                       {decisions.subanalysis.decision1}
  {inputs}             the paths of all the output's inputs, in
                       the order of `inputs`, separated by spaces
  {output}             the path the result is written to

Every brace belongs to a `{{`, a `}}` or a placeholder, every placeholder takes one of these forms, and the <entry> of an {inputs.<entry>} or {decisions.<entry>} is an entry of the output's `inputs` or `decisions`, exactly as written.

Recipe.title: Recipe

Resources.description: Compute resource requirements for a recipe. Values follow cloud-native conventions (string-with-units for sized quantities) so cluster executors can consume them directly.

cpus.description: CPU cores requested. Fractional values are allowed (e.g., 0.5) for runners that support CPU shares.

disk.description: Disk requirement as a string with units (e.g., '10Gi', '500Mi').

memory.description: Memory requirement as a string with units (e.g., '16Gi', '512Mi', '8GB').

time_limit.description: Maximum wall time as a duration string (e.g., '2h', '30m', '1h30m').

Resources.title: Resources

Result.description: A planned result: one output's, in the universe it is built in or, for an output built once, once. Its recipe is its output's, in `fields`.

additionalProperties.description: The id of the option selected where the result is built.

decisions.description: What the result is made with: for each entry of its output's `decisions`, the option selected where the result is built.

inputs.description: What the result reads: one item for each entry of its output's `inputs`, in their order.

output.description: The output the result is of, never a switch.

owner.description: The analysis the result belongs to: the one whose universe builds it or, for an output built once, the one whose output it is.

places.description: Where the result goes, one item for each of its names, in the order the names are reached. The recipe writes the first.

universe.description: The id of the universe the result is built in, one of its owner's. Left out for an output built once.

Result.title: Result

SelectedOption.description: A decision, named by its analysis and id, and the option a universe selects for it.

analysis.description: The analysis the element is in.

id.description: The element's id in that analysis.

in_play.description: Whether the decision is in play in the universe, as the specification defines it. Constraints ignore a decision that isn't.

option.description: The id of the option the universe's effective selection selects, after inheritance through `derived_from`.

SelectedOption.title: SelectedOption

TextQuoteSelector.description: W3C TextQuoteSelector for locating text in a document. The authoritative anchor for verification.

exact.description: The passage, exactly as the cited work or output writes it.

TextQuoteSelector.title: TextQuoteSelector

Through.description: A switch an entry reads through, and the option that picks the case it takes.

option.description: The id of the option selected, in the universe the switch is read in, for the decision it switches on. The case taken is that option's entry of the switch's `cases`.

Through.title: Through

UniverseEntry.description: A universe, named by its analysis and id, and the option it selects for each decision. An import has no entry: the universe it imports has one.

analysis.description: The analysis the element is in.

decisions.description: One item for each decision the universe's effective selection sets, of its own analysis or of another, in the order of the document's `analyses`, then as written in each file. A decision with no item is neither set nor in play.

id.description: The element's id in that analysis.

UniverseEntry.title: UniverseEntry

Universe__identifier_optional.description: An entry of `universes`: a universe of the analysis, a selection of one option for every decision it uses of the analysis and of every analysis, declared directly or not, that the analysis's universes drive, or an import, which has an `analysis` and a `universe`, names one of another analysis's universes and selects nothing. A universe's effective selection is the effective selection of the universe it is derived from, if any, with its own `decisions` written over it decision by decision.

analysis.description: For an import, the address of the declaration that leads to the analysis whose universe it imports, through as many declarations as lead to it, such as `subanalysis` or `stage.inner`.

additionalProperties.description: The id of the option selected for the decision.

decisions.description: The options the universe selects, as `<decision>: <option>`, one key per decision. Each key is the id of a decision of the analysis or, for a decision of another analysis, a flat key: the decision's address through the declarations, `<declaration>.<decision>`, such as `subanalysis.decision1`, or another spelling of that address, through no declaration back to an analysis already on its chain.

derived_from.description: The id of another universe of the analysis, never an import, whose effective selection this universe's effective selection is built on, so that this universe gives only the decisions it changes. The universe inherits only that selection.

description.description: What the universe is, in free prose.

label.description: A short display name for the universe.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the universe.

universe.description: For an import, the id of the universe it imports: a universe of the analysis that `analysis` leads to, never an import of that analysis.

Universe__identifier_optional.title: Universe

description: A valid analysis, resolved: what it and every analysis it declares hold, what each universe selects, and which results are to be built, from what. It is always whole.

analyses.description: The driving analysis, then every analysis it declares, directly or not, in the order they are reached, each identity once.

evidence.description: Every item of the driving analysis's evidence that cites an output, and each item of another analysis that cites a planned result, in the order of `analyses`, then as written in each file.

notes.description: What an author may want to tidy, grouped by kind.

results.description: The planned results, each after every result it reads: an order a runner can build them in.

shape.description: The name and version of the document's shape.

universes.description: Every universe of the driving analysis, in the order written, then each universe of another analysis that a planned result is built in or that a pin reached by the driving analysis names.

title: documents
